trigger_design:
WHERE IT LIVES: A new standalone component web-react/src/components/SubscriptionWelcomeModal.js, mounted in App.js (~line 2628, immediately BEFORE LessonBox, inside the same `loggedinUser !== '0' &&` IIFE guard). It is z-index 10000 and renders OVER everything, including the LessonBox, so it is genuinely the user's FIRST screen after a subscription event. While it is visible it should set LessonBox's `hidden` prop true (reuse the existing `infoBoxVisible` lift or a new `subWelcomeVisible` state) so the daily lesson box never competes with it. When the user closes it, hand off: if the lesson arc has never run, fire `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('tw-lessonbox-open'))` so the LessonBox opens to its new "what these daily lessons are" intro.

THE GLOBAL THAT MUST BE ADDED (operator/deploy item): The client today only sees window.tw2_user_tier, which is the EFFECTIVE (trial-elevated) tier from effective_tier(u) at web/app.py:1505. A just-subscribed explorer (DB tier now 'analyst') is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a reverse-trial explorer (DB tier 'explorer', effective 'strategist') unless the raw DB tier is exposed. So web/app.py must inject a new global next to the others (~line 1626 in the /app index route):  window.tw2_user_tier_actual = <_js_safe(u.tier)>  -- the RAW users.tier ('explorer'|'navigator'|'analyst'|'strategist'|'canceled'), NOT effective_tier(). This is the ONE server change the dialog depends on. All other globals it needs already exist: window.current_user_id, window.tw2_user_tier (effective), window.tw2_trial_ends_at, window.tw2_trial_ever.

WHEN IT FIRES (priority order, evaluated once on /app mount after auth, loggedinUser !== '0'):
  Let ACTUAL = window.tw2_user_tier_actual || window.tw2_user_tier (fall back to effective only if the new global is missing, so the dialog degrades safely pre-deploy).
  Let LAST = localStorage 'tw_last_welcomed_tier' (user-scoped via Common.lsGet, which already prefixes window.current_user_id).
  Let params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).

  (A) HARD SIGNAL from the Stripe redirect (highest priority, fires even if storage already matches - covers re-subscribe to the same tier and cleared storage):
      - params has 'upgraded=1'  -> event = 'upgrade' if ACTUAL > LAST (or LAST unknown and ACTUAL is paid), else a generic paid welcome. Strip the param from the URL (history.replaceState) after reading so a refresh does not re-fire.
      - params has 'welcome=trial' -> event = 'new_signup' (trial). Strip the param.
    The redirect targets come straight from /stripe/success at web/app.py:2363 (`/app/?welcome=trial` for trial subs, `/app/?upgraded=1` for paid). These are the only signal the server sends today; consume them.

  (B) STATE-DIFF fallback (no query param, e.g. user navigated away and back, or paid via a path that did not carry the param):
      - LAST is empty/null:
          * if window.tw2_trial_ever === '1' AND window.tw2_trial_ends_at is non-empty (active reverse trial) -> event = 'new_signup' (trial copy).
          * else if ACTUAL is a paid tier -> event = 'new_signup' (paid copy, no trial clock).
          * else (ACTUAL === 'explorer', no trial) -> DO NOT show (a returning free/expired user is not a welcome moment).
      - LAST is set and ACTUAL !== LAST:
          * rank(ACTUAL) > rank(LAST) -> event = 'upgrade'. SPECIAL CASE: LAST was a trial-elevated 'strategist' record and ACTUAL is a real paid tier below it (analyst/navigator) - treat as a TRIAL -> PAID conversion, use the 'upgrade'/new paid copy for ACTUAL, never 'downgrade' (the user just paid; do not punish them). To detect this, persist a small flag alongside LAST: store the tuple {tier, wasTrial} so a stored trial-strategist does not read as a downgrade when they convert to analyst.
          * rank(ACTUAL) < rank(LAST) and NOT the trial->paid case -> event = 'downgrade'.
          * ACTUAL === 'canceled' -> event = 'downgrade' (back to explorer copy, "what you keep").
      - LAST === ACTUAL -> no-op (idempotent; the same tier seen twice never re-fires).

  rank() order (low->high): explorer(0) < navigator(1) < analyst(2) < strategist(3). Source: web/tier_compat.py:25-32, config.py:635-695.

AVOIDING RE-SHOW: After the dialog is closed (or auto-dismissed), write localStorage 'tw_last_welcomed_tier' = JSON {tier: ACTUAL, wasTrial: (window.tw2_trial_ends_at !== '')}. Because lsSet is user-scoped, a second account on the same browser keeps its own last-welcomed tier. The query-param path also replaceState-strips the param so a manual refresh is a no-op. Net: shows exactly once per real tier transition, robust across storage clears (param is the safety net) and across navigation (state-diff is the safety net).

DO NOT CONFLATE with the existing onboarding cookies: the existing 'tw_welcomed' cookie (onboarding.js:279) gates the OLD trial welcome modal and the LessonBox intro - leave it alone. This new dialog uses its OWN key 'tw_last_welcomed_tier' so the two systems do not fight. On a brand-new signup BOTH may want to fire; let this subscription dialog win (z-index, fires first), and on its close hand off to the LessonBox.

RELATED UI CHANGES THIS WORK SHIPS WITH (not the dialog itself, but the owner's items 2-4):
  2. LessonBox Day 1 / Screen 1 (onboardingLessons.js:23-31) STOPS being the welcome (the real welcome now lives in this dialog). Repurpose it to describe what the daily lessons ARE - see the component_spec field for the exact replacement copy.
  3. On LessonBox close (LessonBox.js closeBox() ~line 238), the toolbar lightbulb (DesktopLayout.js:519-530) should draw the eye: add a CSS pulse/glow class to the bulb span on first close (gate on the existing 'tw_lesson_hintseen' flag), reusing the twLbPulse keyframes; fallback inline line "To open it again, click the lightbulb at the upper left."
  4. LessonBox Back/Next text buttons (LessonBox.js:710-750) become chevron icons: import FaAngleLeft, FaAngleRight from 'react-icons/fa' (already used in OppTable.js:72-86) and render `<FaAngleLeft/>` / `<FaAngleRight/>` instead of the words.
component_spec:
FILE: web-react/src/components/SubscriptionWelcomeModal.js (new standalone component, mirrors OnboardingWelcome.js so it stays visually identical to the rest of the dark "Instrument" surface).

PROPS: { UITheme, rdd, tier, subscriptionEvent ('new_signup'|'upgrade'|'downgrade'), onClose }. tier is the ACTUAL tier resolved by the trigger; for the explorer-trial case pass tier='explorer-trial' (active reverse trial) so it selects the trial copy block, not the free-explorer block.

LOOK (match OnboardingWelcome.js / LessonBox tokens exactly):
  - Full-screen cover at z-index 10000 with a dimmed scrim (rgba(10,10,14,0.72)) and the same fade/scale-in animation OnboardingWelcome uses; centered card.
  - Card: dark Instrument panel - background a near-black gradient (the same C.panel / C.violetDeep tokens LessonBox.js uses), 1px hairline border C.hair, ~18px radius, soft violet drop-shadow (drop-shadow(0 0 24px rgba(167,139,250,0.25))). Responsive width: clamp around 'min(92vw, 460px)'.
  - A small tier badge / eyebrow at the top in the violet accent: the plan name in caps letter-spaced (EXPLORER TRIAL / NAVIGATOR / ANALYST / STRATEGIST). For a downgrade, the eyebrow reads "PLAN UPDATED"; for an upgrade "YOU'VE UPGRADED"; for new_signup "WELCOME".
  - Headline: AP Title Case, no terminal period, the copy_by_tier headline for (tier x event). ~22-26px, weight 600, off-white.
  - Body: one short paragraph, sentence case, the copy_by_tier body for (tier x event). ~15px, line-height 1.5, muted off-white (C.ink70 or similar).
  - Optional: a single thin "what you unlocked" line under the body for upgrade/new (e.g. small violet-bulleted "Now open: futures, forex, bonds, crypto"), pulled from the tier's unlocks summary, kept to ONE line; omit for downgrade (use the body's "what you keep" instead).
  - NO em-dashes anywhere (use ' - '); headlines never end in a period; this is enforced by the copy above.

CTAs (one primary, one quiet secondary - same button styling as LessonBox):
  - PRIMARY (gradient violet, linear-gradient(135deg, C.violet, C.violetDeep), the LessonBox tw-lb-primary style):
      * new_signup (trial): "Start the 7-Day Lessons" - on click: onClose(), then dispatch 'tw-lessonbox-open' so the LessonBox opens to its new lessons-intro screen.
      * new_signup (paid) / upgrade: "Show Me Around" - same handoff (opens the LessonBox intro), OR "Take Me to the Markets" which just closes onto the app if the lessons already ran.
      * downgrade: "Got It" - just onClose(); no lesson handoff (these users are not new).
  - SECONDARY (transparent, 1px C.hair border - the LessonBox "Back" style):
      * new_signup / upgrade: "Explore on My Own" -> onClose() only, no lesson handoff. The toolbar lightbulb pulse (item 3) then teaches them how to reopen lessons.
      * downgrade: omit (single button is plenty).
  - A small top-right close glyph (x) that calls onClose() and is equivalent to the secondary action.

HANDOFF TO THE LESSONBOX SERIES (this is the key integration):
  - This dialog is now THE welcome; the LessonBox is the curriculum. So Day 1 / Screen 1 of the LessonBox (onboardingLessons.js:23-31) must STOP being a second welcome and instead say what the daily lessons are.
  - REPLACEMENT for onboardingLessons.js Day 1 Screen 1 (keep the same shape - title/lead/bullets/pointer):
        title: "What These Daily Lessons Are"
        lead:  "Quick thing before you dig in. This little box is your seven-day guide - one short lesson a day, each one building on the last, walking you through how to actually read what's here."
        bullets: [
          "One bite a day - scanning, then validating, then building a position.",
          "Tara, your analyst, walks each one with you.",
          "Closed it? The lightbulb up top reopens it any time."
        ]
        pointer: ""
    (Day 1 Screens 2 and 3 stay as the "your job this week" / "open the table" hands-on screens; only Screen 1 changes from welcome to lessons-intro.)
  - On the dialog's primary CTA for a NEW user, onClose() then window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('tw-lessonbox-open')) drops them straight onto this new intro screen, so the two surfaces read as one continuous welcome -> "here's your guide" flow with no duplicate "Welcome to TradeWave".

GUARDS / EDGE CASES:
  - Mount inside the `loggedinUser !== '0'` IIFE in App.js (~line 2628), BEFORE <LessonBox/>, and pass LessonBox `hidden` while this is visible so they never stack.
  - Render nothing (return null) when the trigger decides 'no-op' (same tier, or returning free user) - the parent only mounts it when subscriptionEvent is set.
  - 'canceled' actual tier -> treat as explorer for copy selection, event 'downgrade' ("Welcome Back to Explorer").
  - If window.tw2_user_tier_actual is missing (pre-deploy), the component still works off effective tier but cannot tell trial-strategist from paid-strategist; that is the reason the actual-tier global is a required deploy item (see trigger_design).
  - Voice rule baked into every string: warm, human, confident about the historical evidence, never an AI tone, never a profit/returns promise, never advice. Headlines AP Title Case with no terminal period; body sentence case; no em-dashes.

copy_by_tier.unlocks: The 7-day reverse trial: full Strategist access for 7 days - all 15 markets, ML scoring, every saved pattern. After day 7 the free Explorer plan keeps the Dow 30, one portfolio, five tracked opportunities, and everything you already saved.

new.headline: You're In - Seven Days, Full Access
new.body: Welcome aboard, and thanks for trusting us with a week. For the next seven days you have everything: all 15 markets, the ML scores, the long-hold tools, the lot. No card on file, nothing to cancel. Poke at it hard. Find one window worth watching - that is the whole goal. Anything you save stays yours after day seven, even on the free plan, so build like it counts.

upgrade.headline: You're In - Seven Days, Full Access
upgrade.body: Welcome aboard. The next seven days are the full Strategist plan, on the house - every market, every tool, no card on file. Use them to find a real opportunity, not just to click around. Whatever you save is yours to keep when the week ends.

downgrade.headline: Welcome Back to Explorer
downgrade.body: You're on the free Explorer plan now, and you keep more than you'd think: the Dow 30, your saved patterns, one portfolio, and five tracked opportunities. Nothing you built disappears. When you want the rest of the markets back, the door is open and it takes about a minute.

copy_by_tier.unlocks: Navigator ($19/mo): the Dow 30 plus the NASDAQ 100 and the S&P 500, any start date unlocked, up to 50 patterns per market, 3 portfolios, 25 tracked opportunities.

new.headline: Welcome to Navigator
new.body: Glad to have you on Navigator. You just went from the Dow to the three indexes that move the US market - Dow, NASDAQ and S&P 500 - with any start date unlocked, not just today. Start with the Opportunity Table on a fresh market and read down from the top. The strongest seasonal window is the one sitting first. Want the AI-calibrated score on top of the history? That starts at Analyst.

upgrade.headline: Welcome to Navigator
upgrade.body: Nice - you're on Navigator now. The NASDAQ 100 and the S&P 500 just opened up next to the Dow, and you can browse any start date, not just today. More names, same simple read: strongest opportunity on top. Analyst is the next step up if you want the AI-calibrated score riding along.

downgrade.headline: You're on Navigator Now
downgrade.body: You've moved to Navigator, and here's what stays with you: the Dow, NASDAQ and S&P 500, any start date unlocked, three portfolios, and everything you've already saved. The markets above this tier are paused, not gone - one click brings them back whenever you want them.

copy_by_tier.unlocks: Analyst ($47/mo): all U.S. stock groups plus ETFs, ML scoring, SMN research articles, weekly Q&A, 25 portfolios, 100 published date-range reports, and 10 watchlists with 50 symbols each.

new.headline: Welcome to Analyst
new.body: Welcome to Analyst - this is where the toolkit really opens up. You can scan every U.S. stock group plus ETFs, with the AI-calibrated score alongside the historical record. SMN research and the weekly Q&A are open too. Start by scoring a stock or ETF that was outside your previous plan.

upgrade.headline: Welcome to Analyst
upgrade.body: Good move - Analyst suits you. You now have every U.S. stock group plus ETFs, the AI-calibrated score, SMN research articles, and a seat at the weekly Q&A. Open a stock or ETF that was outside your previous plan and put the model next to the full historical record.

downgrade.headline: You're on Analyst Now
downgrade.body: You've settled onto Analyst, and it keeps the parts most people use every day: every U.S. stock group plus ETFs, ML scoring, SMN research, and the weekly Q&A. Futures, forex, bonds, foreign indices and crypto are paused, and your saved work is all still here. Step back up any time you need the full set.

copy_by_tier.unlocks: Strategist ($129/mo): all 15 markets, including futures, forex, bonds, foreign indices and crypto - 100 portfolios, up to 500 published date-range reports, 50 watchlists with 100 symbols each, the weekly Zoom session and premium support.

new.headline: Welcome to Strategist
new.body: Welcome to Strategist - you have the whole engine now. Every one of the 15 markets is open, from U.S. stocks through futures, forex, bonds, foreign indices and crypto. You also have 100 portfolios, up to 500 published date-range reports, and the live weekly Zoom. Best first move: run a scan somewhere you've never been.

upgrade.headline: Welcome to Strategist
upgrade.body: There it is - the full plan. Futures, forex, bonds, foreign indices and crypto just joined everything you already had, so all 15 markets are open. You also have 100 portfolios, up to 500 published date-range reports, and the live weekly Zoom. Go somewhere new and let the history surprise you.

downgrade.headline: Welcome to Strategist
downgrade.body: You're on Strategist now, with every market open - futures, forex, bonds, foreign indices, crypto and all the rest - plus 100 portfolios, up to 500 published date-range reports, and the live weekly Zoom. Everything you'd saved is right where you left it. This is the full toolkit, no corners cut.
